title: U.S. House · New York's 9th Congressional District
area: Central Brooklyn, including Flatbush, East Flatbush, Crown Heights, Midwood, and Park Slope.

context.text: Incumbent Yvette D. Clarke defeated Michael Goldfarb and Joshua Bristol in the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary, 68.4% to 15.4% to 14.9%. Joel Anabilah-Azumah advanced unopposed from the canceled Republican and Conservative Party primaries; Joshua Kaitan Lucas was disqualified from the district's Republican primary, and Lewis Mizrahi and Jean Depalis were disqualified from its Conservative Party primary.

candidates.name: Yvette D. Clarke
candidates.ballotNote: Won the June 23, 2026 Democratic primary with 68.4% of the vote

summary.text: Yvette D. Clarke is the incumbent U.S. Representative for NY-9 and a senior member of the House Energy and Commerce Committee. A Brooklyn native who succeeded her mother on the New York City Council, she has served in Congress since 2007, first for the 11th District and, since 2013, for the 9th. Her official biography highlights work on technology and media policy, health legislation for women, and Caribbean-American issues.

background.text: Born November 21, 1964, in Flatbush, Brooklyn, to Jamaican immigrant parents; her official biography describes her as the daughter of Jamaican immigrants and says she grew up in Flatbush, where she still lives.

Attended Oberlin College from 1982 to 1986 according to Ballotpedia; her official biography describes her as an Oberlin graduate and a recipient of the APPAM/Sloan Fellowship in Public Policy and Policy Analysis, and lists honorary degrees from the University of Technology, Jamaica and the University of the Commonwealth Caribbean.
Before entering elected office, served as director of business development for the Bronx Empowerment Zone (BOEDC).

Served on the New York City Council from 2000 to 2007 for the 40th District in Brooklyn, succeeding her mother, Council Member Una S. T. Clarke, in what her official biography says was the first mother-daughter succession in the Council's history.

Took office in the U.S. House in 2007 representing New York's 11th Congressional District; has represented the 9th District since the 2013 redistricting. She is a member of the Congressional Black Caucus, which her official biography says she chairs.

Sits on the House Energy and Commerce Committee, where her 2025-2026 subcommittee assignments are Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade; Communications and Technology; and Oversight and Investigations. In the 117th Congress she chaired the Homeland Security subcommittee on Cybersecurity, Infrastructure Protection, and Innovation.

Co-chairs the Congressional Caribbean Caucus, Smart Cities Caucus, Multicultural Media Caucus (which she formed), Caucus on Black Women and Girls, and Medicare for All Caucus, according to her official biography.

Her official biography lists, among her 118th Congress legislation, the DEEPFAKES Accountability Act, the REAL Political Ads Act, the Menopause Research Equity Act, and the Stephanie Tubbs Jones Uterine Fibroid and Education Act.
Is an active member of the Brooklyn Alumnae Chapter of Delta Sigma Theta Sorority, Inc., and lives in Flatbush, according to her official biography.

positions.summary: In a September 2026 statement on the Hyde Amendment, called for ensuring affordable abortion care access and criticized the overturning of Roe v. Wade.
positions.quote: That starts with passing the EACH Act and ensuring that every American can access affordable abortion care, no matter what.

positions.summary: In a May 2025 committee markup, opposed Republican reconciliation cuts to Medicaid, calling the program a lifeline for her constituents.
positions.quote: It’s not just policy, but a lifeline for Americans in my district and across the nation.

positions.summary: Describes herself as an advocate for strengthening gun laws and says she will keep pushing for gun legislation.
positions.quote: As an advocate for gun safety and the strengthening of gun laws,  I will continue to advocate for common sense gun legislation to make our communities safer.

positions.summary: In a 2023 statement, objected to Republican efforts to eliminate climate programs created by the Inflation Reduction Act.
positions.quote: At this pivotal moment in our fight against the climate crisis, it’s unacceptable for Republicans to eliminate significant climate programs passed under the Inflation Reduction Act and eviscerate environmental protections that help protect the health and safety of our communities.

record.text: For the 2025-2026 (119th Congress) session, serves on the Committee on Energy and Commerce, including its Commerce, Manufacturing, and Trade subcommittee, its Communications and Technology subcommittee, and its Oversight and Investigations subcommittee.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 9733, the Interagency Council on Affordable Housing Act of 2026, introduced July 16, 2026.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 9014, the Affordable Housing and Area Median Income Fairness Act of 2026.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 9090, the Advancing Menopause Care and Mid-Life Women's Health Act.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 10489, the American Renewable Energy Act of 2026.
Prime sponsor of H.R. 8811, the Moms Matter Act, and H.R. 9457, the Diversity Visa Protection and Modernization Act, in the 119th Congress.

candidates.name: Joel Anabilah-Azumah

summary.text: Joel Anabilah-Azumah is a small-business owner in the transportation field and the Republican and Conservative Party nominee for NY-9 in 2026. He has been a candidate in the district before, appearing on the 2018 and 2020 general election ballots on minor-party lines. In his Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey he lists his focus areas as personal freedom, transportation, and infrastructure, and says he opposes outsourcing government functions to artificial intelligence and U.S. involvement in unnecessary military conflicts.

background.text: Born in New York, New York; earned a bachelor's degree from Union College in 2005, and his career experience is in transportation.
Describes himself in his Ballotpedia survey responses as a small-business owner.
Ran for NY-9 in 2018 on the Reform Party line (779 votes, 0.4%) and in 2020 on the Serve America Movement Party line (1,052 votes, 0.4%), both against Clarke.

In 2022 he was interviewed by PoliticsNY as a Republican candidate for NY-9, where he said he would focus on medical freedom, nutrition education, and increased access to public transportation; Ballotpedia lists him among withdrawn or disqualified candidates for the 2022 U.S. Senate race (as an Independent) and for the 2024 NY-9 race.
Advanced as the Republican and Conservative Party nominee for NY-9 in 2026 after both primaries were canceled.

priorities.text: "I will fight all attempts to outsource government functions to artificial intelligence. Humans must be in charge of governing other humans at all times."
"I will resist all attempts to drag the United States into unnecessary and unwinnable military conflicts."
"I will ensure that citizens of the United States have the ability to speak freely, even when their statements are unpopular."

positions.summary: Campaign website states the federal minimum wage should rise from $7.25 to $17 per hour.
positions.quote: it is my position that the federal minimum wage has to increase from $7.25/hour to $17/hour.

candidates.researchNotes: Anabilah-Azumah has not held elected office, so there is no official governing record to cite.
